phrase.text: An array is a row (or a table) of boxes of the same type, with a fixed size and numbered from zero.

runs.text: How it works
creates the array and its boxes at once. Each box is used like a variable: it is assigned a value and read with the name and the index in brackets. Indices start at
zero
: an array of size 3 has boxes 0, 1 and 2.

blocks.description: Four boxes in a row with the values 7, 9, 6 and 8 and the indices 0, 1, 2 and 3 below. On the right, a fifth dashed, crossed-out box with index 4, which does not exist.

caption.text: An array of size 4 has boxes 0 to 3. Box 4 does not exist.

blocks.title: The week's grades

runs.text: An array can have several
dimensions
. A table with 2 rows and 3 columns is declared with two sizes and each box is named with two indices inside the same brackets:

blocks.title: A small multiplication table

runs.text: Dimensioning in two steps
Classic pseudocode first declares the variable with
and then dimensions it with
without repeating the type. PseudoLearn accepts this if the variable is not used between the two statements.
An array is not a value
A whole array cannot be assigned, compared, written or returned. Only its boxes are values. To pass it whole to a subroutine an array parameter is used, which shares the boxes.

entries.text: Indices: integers from 0 to size − 1 in each dimension.
Size 0: valid (an array with no boxes). Negative size:
Sizes are computed when running, so they can be expressions.
There is no maximum fixed by the language; the limit is the memory available to the engine.

runs.text: Going outside the array stops the program at that access:

blocks.title: The box that does not exist

diagnostics.message: Index 3 is out of range for an array of size 3

runs.text: Using a number of indices different from the number of dimensions is detected before running:

blocks.title: One index short

diagnostics.message: Incorrect number of indices for array m

runs.text: And a whole array cannot be written:

blocks.title: Writing the whole array

diagnostics.message: An array cannot be used as a scalar value in an expression or assignment

runs.text: In the intermediate representation, accessing a box is an instruction that checks the index before reading or writing. If the index is out of range, the instruction produces the trap
with the exact position of the access.
The classic mistake is going from 1 to N instead of 0 to N − 1. Write the
loop with
and look at the failure it produces: the message says which index and which size.

points.text: creates a fixed-size array of boxes of the same type.
Indices go from 0 to size − 1; several indices go inside the same brackets.
Going out of range is a runtime failure.
A whole array is not a value: it is not assigned, compared or written.
